analysis: Examined two benchmark-only changes in the ProviderBenchmark target. (1) ModelBenchmarkNativeQwen4.swift head lines 38-40 add model_type "flint" to usesNativeGeneration. A flint model now takes the native CBv2 path in runNativeQwen4 (head lines 63-154). That path was already used by the other native families: it verifies the WeightHasher hash twice, checks bindRuntimeMetallibForMLX and selfBinaryHash, sets DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=0, and passes requirePersistentKey:false. The change is a pure routing addition that only narrows which scalar generation path runs, and it adds no new trust boundary or auth path. The flint-specific implementation (EngineV2Factory, model registration) is outside the supplied evidence. (2) ThroughputSweep.swift (patch hunk at head lines 123-132 and the new measuresScalarPrefill helper near 203-209) reads config.json to get modelType and skips the scalar prefill sweep for flint. Reading config.json is the same operator-local file read the function already performs via EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.resolve at base lines 77-80. A malformed config would already have thrown earlier, so there is no new failure surface. The skip only produces an empty prefill array and a log line. It does not touch the cache, keys, attestation or the coordinator wire. Neither change touches the production serving path, the prefix cache or SSD tier (T-041), the attestation chain, App Attest authorization or coordinator-provider crypto. The benchmark disables the prefix cache, so there is no at-rest artifact. Threat-model relevance is minimal (TB-007 only incidentally). Remaining question: whether flint is correctly gated and served in production lies in unchanged code that was not supplied, and it is not asserted here.
